1) the RST approach is suitable to detect hot spots, ash clouds and volcanic plumes, and to discriminate them from weather clouds; 2) RST can be applied in real time to satellite data, with a high degree of reliability, and with the potential of being integrated in an Early Warning System (EWS) devoted to volcanic hazard mitigation; 3) the RST technique can be exported to other satellite data sets, with a further improvement of the detection performances.

the Robust Satellite Techniques approach has shown high performance in detecting hot spots and in automatically identifying ash clouds, and that the potential of RST for volcanic hazard monitoring has been proved.

the RST technique is a promising tool for volcanic hazard monitoring, thanks to the possibility of providing automatic detection of hotspots and ash plumes, and that the use of improved satellite systems (i.e., MSG-SEVII and MODIS) is expected to improve the performances of RST, thus increasing its potential for operational use.
